source.quote: An independent three-edge star with distinct terminals a,b,c cannot have boundary-connectivity law assigning probability 1/2 to a|b|c and 1/2 to abc and zero to each pair-only partition.

independent_derivation: Positive triple probability excludes zero arms; zero pair-only masses force all arms to one, contradicting the triple probability. Details in ADVERSARY.md.
remaining_gap: Neither the exact finite obstruction nor this audit proves the scaling-limit target.

scope: finite undirected independent-bond graphs; quantitative bound is for a fixed optional-edge budget

source.quote: If both the all-separated partition and the all-connected partition have positive probability, at least one strictly intermediate terminal partition has positive probability.

independent_derivation: A supported Boolean path adding one optional edge at a time moves from separated to connected. A single edge merges at most two components, so for k>=3 an intermediate partition occurs with positive mass; under the probability floor its mass is at least epsilon^m. This is a separately derived proof, recorded in ADVERSARY.md.
remaining_gap: No uniform obstruction to approximating by growing gadgets; no continuum comparison.

source.quote: their connection-to-b crossing probabilities differ by (2-sqrt(2))/4.

independent_derivation: Inclusion-exclusion: selector crossing is 1/2; star crossing is 2s^2-s^3 with s=1/sqrt(2), giving the stated exact difference.
remaining_gap: A finite pair-marginal counterexample does not refute conformal invariance.
